stories.title: Village's concern over sewage discharge in dry river
summary: Campaigners call for restrictions on sewage treatment plant discharging effluent during drought

stories.title: A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way
summary: A surprising discovery suggests the Milky Way may be making stars in places where most galaxies cannot.
Scientists found evidence that a massive rotating structure near the galactic center is creating powerful shock waves that trigger star formation rather than suppress it.
Even more unexpectedly, part of the Norma spiral arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a vast region where new stars are being born.

stories.title: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation
summary: Astronomers have discovered the oldest known compact pair of quasars, powered by two enormous black holes that existed just 900 million years after the Big Bang.
Weighing an astonishing 1.5 billion and 400 million times the mass of the Sun, these cosmic giants somehow grew to incredible sizes far earlier than current theories can explain.

stories.title: Mysterious new viruses reveal a missing link in evolution
summary: Scientists have discovered previously unknown viruses that could help explain how some of life’s earliest biological structures evolved.
The surprising findings challenge a longstanding evolutionary theory and suggest that viruses may have hidden capabilities far beyond simply infecting cells.

stories.title: Archaeologists reveal a powerful Iron Age king may have been a woman
summary: Archaeologists have uncovered evidence that Verica, the Iron Age ruler whose exile helped trigger Rome’s invasion of Britain in AD 43, was actually a woman.
The discovery challenges centuries of historical assumptions and suggests that a largely forgotten female leader may have changed the course of British history.

stories.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
summary: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

stories.title: This tiny spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome 50% larger than a human’s
summary: A tiny California trapdoor spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome roughly 50% larger than a human's, despite being only about the size of a quarter.
Scientists discovered that its enormous genome contains 4.6 billion DNA base pairs and 52 chromosomes, revealing surprising clues about spider evolution.

stories.title: Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years
summary: Medications taken years or even long ago may leave lasting changes in your gut microbiome, according to a study of more than 2,500 people.
Researchers discovered that common drugs, including antidepressants, blood pressure medications, and anxiety treatments, can leave microbial “fingerprints” long after patients stop taking them.
Surprisingly, some anxiety medications had effects comparable to broad-spectrum antibiotics.

stories.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate summit?
summary: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has formally come to an end after countries failed to agree a deal.
